text: Ascites: Ascites is the abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen. Technically, it is more than 25 millilitres of fluid in the peritoneal cavity, although volumes greater than one litre may occur.

Jaundice: Jaundice, also known as icterus, is a yellowish or, less frequently, greenish pigmentation of the skin and sclera due to high bilirubin levels. Jaundice in adults typically indicates the presence of underlying diseases involving abnormal heme metabolism, liver dysfunction, or biliary-tract obstruction.

Neonatal jaundice associated with preterm delivery: Neonatal jaundice, clinically known as neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and icterus neonatorum, is the yellowish discoloration of the white part of the eyes (sclerae) and skin in newborn infants caused by an elevated concentration of bilirubin in the blood (hyperbilirubinemia). It is one of the most frequently encountered medical conditions in the neonatal period, affecting approximately 60% of term and 80% preterm newborns within the first week of life. Common presenting complaints: Jaundice. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
